title: Jean-Marie's songs, theory and the loss of his cello
summary: He discusses his songs with Jean-Marie, public domain status, his interest in theory and conducting, and the burning of his cello around 1922-23.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Past the 28 years, 56 years. You didn't renew it, I guess.

No. I didn't renew it. I didn't renew it. It's in the public domain. Then I put music to another piece that Jean-Marie wrote. It was called Jailhouse Blues. And we found out that somebody else had a Jailhouse Blues. Yes. Bessie Smith made one of the record. Then we have- Then he wrote another one, Lloyd Babe. Lloyd Babe. And I put music to that. And there were several other pieces. There were orchestrated for it. And I got a- I got a- I got a- Chase them up there. I got a lot of music there. I got both classical and jazz and everything else. I got a lot of music. I- Yeah. I don't- Don- But I kept up with that theory of music, you understand? Most so. I got interested in that, and I got interested in interpreting pieces, you know, like conducting orchestras and things like that. And I did more of that in recent years than before, than in doing any playing. And then, unfortunately, I lost my cello. I had a cello that was an heirloom from my mother's family. I don't know why it came. And that was the instrument I learned on. Unfortunately, my friend Mike Neal, the one that I spoke before, was living on Durban Street near the Maine. And when we were playing for Robe Show, we used to rehearse at his house. And his daughter, his oldest daughter, seemed to have taken a liking to the cello. And he asked me would I let the girl use the cello? Well, I let her down. And he had a big fire when nobody was home, and the cello got drunk. Well, it burned up. And I stayed without a cello. Oh, I don't know how long I stayed without a cello. That happened way back then. Which season? Somewhere around 1922, 23. And I stayed without a cello until a friend of mine had a cello, but I don't fool it up because it's, I don't like the tone of it, because it's a school cello. And it seemed as though this man was a friend of a friend of mine. And he wanted to borrow $25. And he gave the cello as a horse. But he never did pay the $25. He never kept with a cello. So my friend gave the cello to me. In fact, he sold it to me. I paid him for it because I had been with a cello so long. So I thought it best to take that or not. I wasn't in a position to go buy an instrument. Because to buy an instrument like I'd want would be very expensive. You know, a cello is not a cheap instrument. So I have it there. And I have my saxophone there. That was made a present to me by my wife, the saxophone. And my whole clarinet is there.
